The '''2023 Telangana Legislative Assembly election''' was held on [[2023 elections in India|30 November 2023]] to elect all [[List of constituencies of the Telangana Legislative Assembly|119 members]] of [[Telangana Legislative Assembly]] for its third term. The votes were counted and the results were declared on 3 December 2023.

The [[Indian National Congress]] (INC) along with its ally [[Communist Party of India]] (CPI) won a majority with 65 seats against the incumbent [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi]] (BRS)'s 39 seats. With a victory for the first time after the formation of Telangana, it strengthened the INC's position in southern India following its recent success in [[2023 Karnataka Legislative Assembly election|Karnataka]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Livemint|date=2023-12-03|title=Telangana Election Results 2023 LIVE: Congress set to solidify its position in Southern India as party maintains lead|url=https://www.livemint.com/elections/assembly-elections/telangana-assembly-election-results-2023-live-updates-check-telangana-vidhan-sabha-chunav-gajwel-kamareddy-sircilla-kcr-11701530430692.html|access-date=2023-12-03|website=mint|language=en|archive-date=9 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209131738/https://www.livemint.com/elections/assembly-elections/telangana-assembly-election-results-2023-live-updates-check-telangana-vidhan-sabha-chunav-gajwel-kamareddy-sircilla-kcr-11701530430692.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The BRS and the outgoing chief minister [[K. Chandrashekar Rao]] suffered a major loss in the elections by losing in one of his contended seats after being in power for two terms.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kurmanath |first=K. V. |date=2023-12-03 |title=Congress clinches Telangana; KCR defeated at Kamareddy |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/congress-clinches-telangana-kcr-defeated-at-kamareddy/article67601603.ece |access-date=2023-12-05 |website=BusinessLine |language=en |archive-date=5 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205122803/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/congress-clinches-telangana-kcr-defeated-at-kamareddy/article67601603.ece |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Background==
The tenure of [[Telangana Legislative Assembly]] was scheduled to end on 16 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Terms of the Houses |url=https://eci.gov.in/elections/term-of-houses/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220328103956/https://eci.gov.in/elections/term-of-houses/ |archive-date=28 March 2022 |access-date=2022-02-13 |website=Election Commission of India |language=en-IN}}</ref> The [[2018 Telangana Legislative Assembly election|previous assembly elections]] were held in December 2018 and the incumbent Telangana Rashtra Samithi, which was later renamed as [[Telangana Rashtra Samithi|Bharat Rashtra Samithi]], formed the [[Government of Telangana|state government]], with [[K. Chandrashekar Rao]] becoming the [[List of chief ministers of Telangana|Chief Minister]] for the second time.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2018-12-13|title=K Chandrashekar Rao takes oath as Telangana Chief Minister for 2nd time|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/131218/k-chandrashekar-rao-oath-taking-telangana-chief-minister-second-time.html|access-date=2022-02-13|website=Deccan Chronicle|language=en|archive-date=13 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220213121518/https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/131218/k-chandrashekar-rao-oath-taking-telangana-chief-minister-second-time.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Schedule==
The election schedule was announced by the [[Election Commission of India]] on 9 October 2023.<ref name="Tela1">{{cite news |date=9 October 2023 |title=Telangana goes to polls on Nov 30, counting on Dec 3 |language=en |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/telangana-elections-2023-telangana-goes-to-polls-on-nov-30-counting-on-dec-3/article67398829.ece |access-date=9 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231009075116/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/telangana-elections-2023-telangana-goes-to-polls-on-nov-30-counting-on-dec-3/article67398829.ece |archive-date=9 October 2023}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite news |date=2023-10-19 |title=Telangana assembly elections 2023 schedule: Important dates, polling and results |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/telangana-election-dates-2023-ts-assembly-election-schedule-polling-results-nominations/articleshow/104274758.cms |access-date=2023-10-23 |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=24 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231024145810/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/telangana-election-dates-2023-ts-assembly-election-schedule-polling-results-nominations/articleshow/104274758.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Election statistics ==
There are 15,871,493 male voters and 15,843,339 female voters while the number of transgender voters stood at 2,557. 2,202,168 voters were deleted across the state.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Telangana Election 2023 Dates, Full Schedule, Results: All You Need to Know |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/assembly-polls/story/telangana-assembly-election-november-30-date-results-2446400-2023-10-09 |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=India Today |language=en |archive-date=29 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231029115029/https://www.indiatoday.in/assembly-polls/story/telangana-assembly-election-november-30-date-results-2446400-2023-10-09 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A total of 2,290 candidates were in the fray, while 608 withdrew their nominations. The highest number of candidates in the electoral contest is from the [[Lal Bahadur Nagar Assembly constituency|L. B. Nagar]] constituency, with 48 candidates, and the least from [[Banswada Assembly constituency|Banswada]] and [[Narayanpet Assembly constituency|Narayanpet]] constituencies, each with 7 candidates.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-11-16 |title=Telangana elections {{!}} 2,290 candidates in fray, 608 withdraw nominations |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/telangana-elections-2290-candidates-in-fray-608-withdraw-nominations/article67539867.ece |access-date=2023-11-16 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130162902/https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/telangana-elections-2290-candidates-in-fray-608-withdraw-nominations/article67539867.ece |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2,290 candidates in fray, 608 withdraw nominations for Telangana polls |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/elections/telangana/2290-candidates-in-fray-608-withdraw-nominations-for-telangana-polls-2773393 |access-date=2023-11-16 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en |archive-date=16 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116170445/https://www.deccanherald.com/elections/telangana/2290-candidates-in-fray-608-withdraw-nominations-for-telangana-polls-2773393 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[Election Commission of India]] seized a total of ₹659.2 crore worth of cash and goods across the state, which were alleged to be used by contesting candidates to influence voters in the elections and conduct general electoral malpractice, in violation of the [[Model Code of Conduct]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-11-20 |title=Seven times more goods and cash to induce voters seized from five poll bound states as compared to 2018 |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/drugs-cash-liquor-worth-over-1760-crore-seized-in-five-poll-going-states-ec/article67553806.ece |access-date=2023-11-21 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=21 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121191050/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/drugs-cash-liquor-worth-over-1760-crore-seized-in-five-poll-going-states-ec/article67553806.ece |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-20 |title=EC seizes over ₹1760 crore from poll-bound states; Rajasthan, Telangana lead |url=https://www.livemint.com/elections/ec-seizes-over-rs-1760-crore-from-poll-bound-states-rajasthan-telangana-lead-list-11700471226319.html |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=mint |language=en |archive-date=21 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121191051/https://www.livemint.com/elections/ec-seizes-over-rs-1760-crore-from-poll-bound-states-rajasthan-telangana-lead-list-11700471226319.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[Indian National Congress]] fought the elections in alliance with the [[Communist Party of India]], whereas the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] fought alongside the [[Janasena Party]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Telangana: Huge number of candidates from smaller parties, besides Independents cause worry among National as well as Regional Parties|url=https://newsonair.gov.in/Main-News-Details.aspx?title=Telangana:-Huge-number-of-candidates-from-smaller-parties,-besides-Independents-cause-worry-among-National-as-well-as-Regional-Parties,-including-BJP-and-Congress&id=471554|access-date=2023-11-24|website=newsonair.gov.in|archive-date=24 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231124134449/https://newsonair.gov.in/Main-News-Details.aspx?title=Telangana:-Huge-number-of-candidates-from-smaller-parties,-besides-Independents-cause-worry-among-National-as-well-as-Regional-Parties,-including-BJP-and-Congress&id=471554|url-status=live}}</ref> The Telangana outfit of the [[Telugu Desam Party]] did not contest.

== Issues ==
=== Kaleshwaram project ===
INC leader [[Rahul Gandhi]] called the [[Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project]], the flagship scheme of the [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi]] government in [[Telangana]], the "ATM of [[K. Chandrashekar Rao|KCR's]] family".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Telangana: Kaleshwaram project is KCR's ATM: Rahul Gandhi at Mahila Sadassu in Telangana |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/elections/assembly-elections/telangana-assembly-elections/kaleshwaram-project-is-kcrs-atm-rahul-gandhi-at-mahila-sadassu-in-telangana/articleshow/104909296.cms |access-date=2023-11-16 |website=[[The Economic Times]] |archive-date=3 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240203235023/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/elections/assembly-elections/telangana-assembly-elections/kaleshwaram-project-is-kcrs-atm-rahul-gandhi-at-mahila-sadassu-in-telangana/articleshow/104909296.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> He made those remarks after visiting the [[Lakshmi Barrage|Medigadda Barrage]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Reddy |first=R. Ravikanth |date=2023-11-02 |title=Rahul Gandhi visits 'sunken pillars' at Medigadda barrage of Kaleshwaram project |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/rahul-gandhi-visits-sunken-pillars-at-medigadda-barrage-of-kaleshwaram-project/article67488377.ece |access-date=2023-11-16 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=16 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116164953/https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/rahul-gandhi-visits-sunken-pillars-at-medigadda-barrage-of-kaleshwaram-project/article67488377.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> which had come under scrutiny of the National Dam Safety Authority after six piers in its seventh block showed signs of damage and leakage.<ref>{{Cite web |title="Useless": Central Panel Slams Telangana Dam, KCR's Party Hits Back |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/medigadda-barrage-sinking-kaleswaram-irrigation-project-telangana-assembly-election-multiple-failures-useless-central-panels-report-on-telangana-dam-4541863 |access-date=2023-11-16 |website=NDTV.com |archive-date=16 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116164952/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/medigadda-barrage-sinking-kaleswaram-irrigation-project-telangana-assembly-election-multiple-failures-useless-central-panels-report-on-telangana-dam-4541863 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-11-04 |title=NDSA report on Medigadda faults design, construction & operation |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/ndsa-report-on-medigadda-faults-design-construction-operation/articleshow/104955074.cms |access-date=2023-11-16 |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=16 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116164952/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/ndsa-report-on-medigadda-faults-design-construction-operation/articleshow/104955074.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Dharani portal ===
The Dharani Portal, an Integrated land records system launched by the incumbent [[Second K. Chandrashekar Rao ministry|BRS government]] as part of its land reform scheme, to aid farmers in the distribution of the [[Rythu Bandhu scheme]], has been contested by opposition parties, who alleged that it was created with the purpose of grabbing the land of poor farmers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KCR's Land Records Portal 'Dharani' Is Latest Poll Issue In Telangana |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/telangana-polls-kcrs-land-records-portal-dharani-is-latest-poll-issue-in-telangana-4562939 |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=NDTV.com |archive-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117045408/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/telangana-polls-kcrs-land-records-portal-dharani-is-latest-poll-issue-in-telangana-4562939 |url-status=live }}</ref> The BJP chief, [[J. P. Nadda]], vowed that the portal would be abolished if the BJP came to power,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-11-10 |title=Telangana polls: BRS government's Dharani portal becomes issue, KCR terms it flawless; BJP, Congress vow to abolish it |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/telangana-polls-brs-governments-dharani-portal-becomes-issue-kcr-terms-it-flawless-bjp-congress-vow-to-abolish-it/articleshow/105116688.cms |access-date=2023-11-17 |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117121804/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/telangana-polls-brs-governments-dharani-portal-becomes-issue-kcr-terms-it-flawless-bjp-congress-vow-to-abolish-it/articleshow/105116688.cms |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-26 |title=BJP will scrap Dharani portal, if voted to power in Telangana: JP Nadda |url=https://www.newstap.in/telangana/bjp-will-scrap-dharani-portal-if-voted-to-power-in-telangana-jp-nadda-1482259 |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=www.newstap.in |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117045406/https://www.newstap.in/telangana/bjp-will-scrap-dharani-portal-if-voted-to-power-in-telangana-jp-nadda-1482259 |url-status=live }}</ref> while the INC promised that they would replace the existing portal with an improved version called 'Bhu Bharati'.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-11 |title=Congress will come up with portal more efficient than Dharani: Revanth Reddy in Bellampalli |url=https://www.newstap.in/telangana/congress-will-come-up-with-portal-more-efficient-than-dharani-revanth-reddy-in-bellampalli-1504107 |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=www.newstap.in |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117045405/https://www.newstap.in/telangana/congress-will-come-up-with-portal-more-efficient-than-dharani-revanth-reddy-in-bellampalli-1504107 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-02 |title=Decoding Politics: What is Telangana's Dharani website that is in the middle of BRS-Congress spat? |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/political-pulse/telangana-dharani-brs-congress-9010821/ |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=The Indian Express |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117050723/https://indianexpress.com/article/political-pulse/telangana-dharani-brs-congress-9010821/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-07-06 |title=Congress comes out with Dharani Declaration with a host of solutions to the present problems |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/congress-comes-out-with-dharani-declaration-with-a-host-of-solutions-to-the-present-problems/article67050250.ece |access-date=2023-11-17 == Incidents ==
===Assassination attempt===
On 30 October 2023, an unidentified man stabbed [[Kotha Prabhakar Reddy]], [[Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha|Member of Parliament]] for [[Medak Lok Sabha constituency|Medak]], in the stomach while posing as if to shake hands with him during a campaign in [[Siddipet district]]. He was apprehended by others in the crowd and put into police custody.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KCR Party MP Stabbed While Campaigning In Telangana, Hospitalised |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/kotha-prabhakar-reddy-stabbed-kcr-party-mp-stabbed-while-campaigning-in-telangana-4527438 |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=NDTV.com |archive-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117051851/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/kotha-prabhakar-reddy-stabbed-kcr-party-mp-stabbed-while-campaigning-in-telangana-4527438 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-30 |title=KCR party MP Kotha Prabhakar Reddy stabbed while campaigning in Telangana's Siddipet |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/telangana-assembly-election-brs-mp-kotha-prabhakar-reddy-stabbed-while-campaigning-in-siddipet-101698657947678.html |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117051852/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/telangana-assembly-election-brs-mp-kotha-prabhakar-reddy-stabbed-while-campaigning-in-siddipet-101698657947678.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Other===
On 16 November 2023, a person, carrying two bullets, was arrested at a public meeting in [[Narsapur Assembly constituency|Narsapur]]. Incumbent [[List of chief ministers of Telangana|Chief Minister of Telangana]], [[K. Chandrashekar Rao]] was in attendance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-17 |title=Hyderabad: Man held for carrying bullets at KCR public meeting in Narsapur |url=https://www.thehansindia.com/news/cities/hyderabad/hyderabad-man-held-for-carrying-bullets-at-kcr-public-meeting-in-narsapur-838335 |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=www.thehansindia.com |language=en |archive-date=21 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121193034/https://www.thehansindia.com/news/cities/hyderabad/hyderabad-man-held-for-carrying-bullets-at-kcr-public-meeting-in-narsapur-838335 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-16 |title=Police Find Two Bullets at CM KCR's Meeting |url=https://www.m9.news/short/police-find-two-bullets-at-cm-kcrs-meeting/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=M9.news |language=en-US |archive-date=9 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250409170914/https://www.m9.news/short/police-find-two-bullets-at-cm-kcrs-meeting/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bullets at CM KCR s Rally: YouTube Channel Reporter.? |url=http://www.indiaherald.com/Breaking/Read/994650086/Bullets-at-CM-KCRs-Rally-YouTube-Channel-Reporter |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=indiaherald.com |language=en |archive-date=21 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121193053/https://www.indiaherald.com/Breaking/Read/994650086/Bullets-at-CM-KCRs-Rally-YouTube-Channel-Reporter |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Campaigns ==
=== Bharat Rashtra Samithi===

Bharat Rashtra Samithi president and Chief Minister [[K. Chandrashekar Rao]] launched the party campaign at an election meeting in [[Husnabad]] on 15 October 2023, where he announced the party manifesto.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sridhar |first=P. |date=2023-10-15 |title=KCR kickstarts BRS election campaign, exhorts party cadres to popularise manifesto |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/kcr-kickstarts-brs-election-campaign-exhorts-party-cadres-to-popularise-manifesto/article67423939.ece |access-date=2023-10-16 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=16 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016060831/https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/kcr-kickstarts-brs-election-campaign-exhorts-party-cadres-to-popularise-manifesto/article67423939.ece |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Chandrashekhar |first=B. |date=2023-10-14 |title=KCR to launch 2023 poll campaign from his lucky venue — Husnabad — on Sunday |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/kcr-to-launch-2023-poll-campaign-from-his-lucky-venue-husnabad-on-sunday/article67421287.ece |access-date=2023-10-16 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=15 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231015070342/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/kcr-to-launch-2023-poll-campaign-from-his-lucky-venue-husnabad-on-sunday/article67421287.ece |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Manifesto====
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) president and Chief Minister [[K. Chandrashekar Rao]] released his party's manifesto on 15 October 2023.<ref name="BRS1">{{cite news |date=15 October 2023 |title=BRS promises monthly honorarium of ₹3,000 for women, superfine rice supply through PDS in manifesto |language=en-IN |url=https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/brs-chief-kcr-releases-the-partys-manifesto-for-telangana-assembly-elections-2023/article67423344.ece |access-date=16 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016071006/https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/brs-chief-kcr-releases-the-partys-manifesto-for-telangana-assembly-elections-2023/article67423344.ece |archive-date=16 October 2023}}</ref><ref name="KCR1">{{cite news |date=16 October 2023 |title=KCR Releases BRS Manifesto For Telangana Assembly Elections at Telangana Bhavan |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/politics/151023/kcr-releases-brs-manifesto-for-telangana-assembly-elections-at-pragath.html |access-date=16 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016072333/https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/politics/151023/kcr-releases-brs-manifesto-for-telangana-assembly-elections-at-pragath.html |archive-date=16 October 2023}}</ref>

'''Social security pension''': Pensions currently stands at ₹2,016, will be increased to ₹3,016 in the first year after the [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi|BRS]] returns to power, and then be raised incrementally up to ₹5,000 in the next four years.

'''Rythu Bandhu scheme''': [[Rythu Bandhu]] scheme in which farmers get ₹10,000 per annum per acre, the payments will be enhanced gradually to ₹16,000 per annum over the next five years.

'''Gas cylinder''': After returning to power [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi|BRS]] will give each gas cylinder at ₹400 to 'eligible beneficiaries' and the remaining cost will be borne by the state government.

'''Arogya Sri health scheme''': ₹1,500,000 health insurance cover to all eligible beneficiaries under the 'Arogya Sri' health scheme, increasing it from the present ₹500,000.

'''Housing''': House sites would be provided to the poor who have no house in the state. The current housing policy will continue.

'''Rice distribution''': Distribute of fine rice through Fair Price shops soon after the party comes to power.

=== Indian National Congress ===
Former President and General Secretary of the [[Indian National Congress|Congress Party]], [[Rahul Gandhi]] and [[Priyanka Gandhi]] launched the Congress campaign at Mulugu on 18 October 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-18 |title=Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra kick off Congress campaign for Telangana Assembly polls; launch bus yatra |url=https://www.news9live.com/state/telangana/rahul-gandhi-priyanka-gandhi-vadra-kick-off-congress-campaign-for-telangana-assembly-polls-launch-bus-yatra-2324591 |access-date=2023-11-24 |website=News9live |language=en-US |archive-date=24 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231124125940/https://www.news9live.com/state/telangana/rahul-gandhi-priyanka-gandhi-vadra-kick-off-congress-campaign-for-telangana-assembly-polls-launch-bus-yatra-2324591 |url-status=live }}</ref> The bus yatra lasted three days and covered eight constituencies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra to launch campaign in poll-bound Telangana with bus yatra on October 18 |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/congress-leaders-rahul-gandhi-and-priyanka-gandhi-vadra-to-launch-campaign-in-poll-bound-telangana-with-bus-yatra-on-october-18/cid/1974101 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Telegraph India |language=en |archive-date=21 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231021073016/https://www.telegraphindia.com/india/congress-leaders-rahul-gandhi-and-priyanka-gandhi-vadra-to-launch-campaign-in-poll-bound-telangana-with-bus-yatra-on-october-18/cid/1974101 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Subsequently, on 30 October 2023 and 3 November 2023, [[Telangana Jana Samithi]] and [[YSR Telangana Party]] respectively announced that they would not contest state elections and instead support the Congress.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-11-03 |title=Sharmila's YSR Telangana Party not to contest elections, to support Congress |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/sharmilas-ysr-telangana-party-not-to-contest-elections-to-support-congress/article67492828.ece |access-date=2023-11-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103161708/https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/sharmilas-ysr-telangana-party-not-to-contest-elections-to-support-congress/article67492828.ece |archive-date=3 November 2023 |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jaiswal |first=Arushi |date=2023-10-30 |title=Telangana Jana Samiti to support Congress in next month Assembly elections |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/telangana/hyderabad-telangana-jana-samiti-support-congress-assembly-elections-m-kodandaram-revanth-reddy-brs-kcr-bjp-latest-updates-2023-10-30-900338 |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=www.indiatvnews.com |language=en |archive-date=21 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121194453/https://www.indiatvnews.com/telangana/hyderabad-telangana-jana-samiti-support-congress-assembly-elections-m-kodandaram-revanth-reddy-brs-kcr-bjp-latest-updates-2023-10-30-900338 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Manifesto ====
Former Congress president [[Sonia Gandhi]] unveiled the party's six guarantees at a rally in [[Tukkuguda]] on 17 September 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-17 |title=Congress unveils six guarantees for poll-bound Telangana |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/congress-unveils-six-guarantees-for-poll-bound-telangana-101694974676273.html |access-date=2023-10-14 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en |archive-date=14 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014152218/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/congress-unveils-six-guarantees-for-poll-bound-telangana-101694974676273.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-17 |title='My dream is to see…': Sonia Gandhi as she announces 6 guarantees for Telangana |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/my-dream-to-see-sonia-gandhi-as-she-announces-6-guarantees-for-telangana-101694959030264.html |access-date=2023-10-14 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en |archive-date=14 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014174959/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/my-dream-to-see-sonia-gandhi-as-she-announces-6-guarantees-for-telangana-101694959030264.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=LPG cylinder for Rs 500, free bus travel: 6 guarantees by Congress in Telangana |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/telangana-assembly-polls-2023/story/lpg-cylinder-for-rs-500-free-bus-travel-6-guarantees-by-congress-in-telangana-2436939-2023-09-17 |access-date=2023-10-15 |website=India Today |date=17 September 2023 |language=en |archive-date=16 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016071320/https://www.indiatoday.in/elections/telangana-assembly-polls-2023/story/lpg-cylinder-for-rs-500-free-bus-travel-6-guarantees-by-congress-in-telangana-2436939-2023-09-17 |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Agriculture''': Farmers and agricultural labourers will receive ₹15,000 and ₹12,000 in financial assistance each year. Bonus of ₹500 per quintal for paddy above minimum support price.

'''Electricity''': 200 free electrical units to all households under the Gruha Jyothi scheme.

'''Housing''': Under the Indiramma Idlu scheme, a piece of land and ₹500,000 for the construction of a house will be provided to the homeless poor. 250 sq. yards plot for families of martyrs of the [[Telangana movement]].

'''Seniors''': ₹4,000 monthly pension for the elderly, widows and others as well as and ₹1,000,000 worth Rajiv Arogyasri insurance cover for poor under the Cheyutha scheme.

'''Women''': Under the Mahalakshmi scheme, women shall receive ₹2,500 every month in financial assistance, gas cylinders for ₹500, and free travel in [[Telangana State Road Transport Corporation|RTC]] buses.

'''Old pension scheme''':
Reimplementation of the Old Pension Scheme, which it did in Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka.

'''Youth''': Vidya Bharosa Card worth ₹500,000 to students for pursuing higher education and establishment of Telangana International School in every mandal (block).

=== Bharatiya Janata Party ===
Bharatiya Janata Party leader [[Amit Shah]] launched the [[Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP's]] campaign at a public meeting in [[Adilabad]] on 10 October 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amit Shah to kick-start poll campaign in Telangana |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/elections/telangana/amit-shah-to-kick-start-poll-campaign-in-telangana-2719686 |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en |archive-date=21 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231021073014/https://www.deccanherald.com/elections/telangana/amit-shah-to-kick-start-poll-campaign-in-telangana-2719686 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Nitin |date=2023-10-10 |title=Telangana Elections 2023: Amit Shah launches BJP's campaign with Adilabad rally, attacks KCR, Congress {{!}} News – India TV |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/telangana/hyderabad-telangana-elections-2023-amit-shah-campaign-adilabad-rally-intellectuals-meet-bjp-leaders-nizamabad-central-tribal-university-pm-modi-2023-10-10-897098 |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=India TV |language=en |archive-date=15 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231015110333/https://www.indiatvnews.com/telangana/hyderabad-telangana-elections-2023-amit-shah-campaign-adilabad-rally-intellectuals-meet-bjp-leaders-nizamabad-central-tribal-university-pm-modi-2023-10-10-897098 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Manifesto ====
[[Minister of Home Affairs (India)|Union Home Minister]] [[Amit Shah]] unveiled the [[Bharatiya Janata Party – Telangana|BJP Telangana]]'s manifesto for Telangana Assembly elections in the name of "Sakala Janula Saubhagya Telangana" on 18 November 2023 in [[Hyderabad]].<ref name="sops">{{cite news |date=18 November 2023 |title=BJP's manifesto for Telangana dodges anti-freebies policy, promises several sops |language=en-IN |url=https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/bjps-manifesto-for-telangana-dodges-anti-freebies-policy-promises-several-sops/article67548286.ece |access-date=19 November 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231119100244/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/telangana/bjps-manifesto-for-telangana-dodges-anti-freebies-policy-promises-several-sops/article67548286.ece |archive-date=19 November 2023}}</ref>

'''Gas cylinder''': The beneficiaries of the Ujjwala Yojana will be given four gas cylinders per year for free.

'''Uniform Civil Code (UCC)''': Once the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] forms government in Telangana, it will, within 6 months, bring the [[Uniform Civil Code]] (UCC) in the State.

'''Hyderabad Liberation Day''': Hyderabad Liberation Day (September 17) and the Razakar Vibhishika Smriti Divas (August 27) will "be celebrated officially by the Government".

'''Zero tolerance against corruption''': Investigate all the cases of corruption through a system headed by the retired Supreme Court judge. It will appoint committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to go into alleged corruption by [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi|BRS]] government.

'''Education & employment''': Those pursuing degree or professional courses will be given free laptops for college girl students, 10 lakh jobs for women, party will ensure that employment is provided to 2.5 youth in the next five years in the state.

'''Reservation''': Abolish unconstitutional religion-based reservations

'''Aada Bidda Bharosa''': Fixed deposit scheme for a girl child at her birth, under which ₹200,000 can be redeemed when she turns 21.

==Results==

The Congress with its ally, the CPI got a clear majority by winning 65 seats. It defeated the incumbent BRS which secured 39 seats. BJP won eight and AIMIM retained its seven seats in the Greater Hyderabad region. The [[Janasena Party]] (JSP), which contested in eight seats as a partner of [[Bharatiya Janata Party]], lost all of them. [[Bahujan Samaj Party]] (BSP) and [[Communist Party of India (Marxist)]] (CPI(M)) lost in all the contested seats. The vote share of [[AIMIM]] is comparatively less due to less voter turnout in their seats.

[[Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee|Telangana PCC]] president [[Revanth Reddy]] was widely credited with the success of his party in the polls.<ref>{{Cite web|title=How Revanth Reddy Changed The Game For Congress In Telangana|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/revanth-reddy-telangana-assembly-election-2023-how-revanth-reddy-changed-the-game-for-congress-in-telangana-4628533|access-date=2023-12-03|website=NDTV.com|archive-date=3 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231203143734/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/revanth-reddy-telangana-assembly-election-2023-how-revanth-reddy-changed-the-game-for-congress-in-telangana-4628533|url-status=live}}</ref> Congress state in-charge Masoor Khan stated that [[Rahul Gandhi]]'s [[Bharat Jodo Yatra]] worked in favour in the Congress in Telangana.<ref>{{Citation|title=Video: Telangana Election Results: Rahul Gandhi's 'Bharat Jodo Yatra' Worked For Congress: Mansoor Khan|url=https://www.ndtv.com/video/news/news/telangana-election-results-rahul-gandhi-s-bharat-jodo-yatra-worked-for-congress-mansoor-khan-743010|access-date=2023-12-03|archive-date=3 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231203143734/https://www.ndtv.com/video/news/news/telangana-election-results-rahul-gandhi-s-bharat-jodo-yatra-worked-for-congress-mansoor-khan-743010|url-status=live}}</ref> The Congress' landslide victory in neighbouring [[Karnataka]] a few months earlier was also emphasised as a major boost for the Congress in the state.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2023-12-03|title=What Congress got right in its sole spark, Telangana|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/political-pulse/what-congress-got-right-telangana-assembly-elections-9052393/|access-date=2023-12-03|website=The Indian Express|language=en|archive-date=3 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231203143329/https://indianexpress.com/article/political-pulse/what-congress-got-right-telangana-assembly-elections-9052393/|url-status=live}}</ref> Congress party poll strategist Sunil Kanugolu was also highlighted in the media for his efforts.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2023-12-03|title=Who is Sunil Kanugolu, Congress poll strategist responsible for historic win in Telangana? |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/who-is-sunil-kanugolu-congress-poll-strategist-responsible-for-historic-win-in-telangana-election-results-2023-kcr-101701596907844.html|access-date=2023-12-03|website=Hindustan Times|language=en}}</ref>

According to an analysis in [[The Hindu]], strong anti-incumbency generated due to the failure to fill government jobs, the arrogant attitude of the Chief Minister, discrepancies in the cash transfer and welfare schemes, general corruption, voter fatigue, [[land grabbing]] charges faced by 30-40 BRS MLAs, and Chandrasekhar Rao's “bold” and early decision of fielding most of the BRS MLAs, including those with a dubious track record helped the Congress in winning the election.<ref>{{Cite news|title=The Congress's great resurgence in Telangana|url=https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/the-congresss-great-resurgence-in-telangana/article67604337.ece|date=2023-12-05|work=The Hindu|url-access=subscription|access-date=5 December 2023|archive-date=5 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205105307/https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/the-congresss-great-resurgence-in-telangana/article67604337.ece|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Results by region ===
Out of the total of 25 seats in the Greater Hyderabad region, [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi|BRS]] won 16, followed by [[All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen|AIMIM]] with 7. [[Indian National Congress|INC]] and [[Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP]] secured one seat each. The INC's victory was on account of its performance in north and south Telangana. 

Out of the total of 51 seats in the North Telangana region, [[Indian National Congress|congress]] won 33, followed by [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi|BRS]] with 10. [[Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP]] secured 7 seats in this region. The INC's victory was on account of its performance in north and south Telangana. [[All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen|AIMIM]] only contested in Greater Hyderabad.<ref name=":6" />

Out of the total of 43 seats in the South Telangana region, [[Indian National Congress|congress]] won 30, followed by [[Bharat Rashtra Samithi|BRS]] with 13. [[Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP]] did not win any seat in this region. The INC's victory was on account of its performance in north and south Telangana. [[All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen|AIMIM]] only contested in Greater Hyderabad.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |title=2023 Telangana Assembly elections - Winds of change in Telangana |url=https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/2023-telangana-assembly-elections-winds-of-change-in-telangana/article67605464.ece |last=Shastri |first=Sandeep |date=2023-12-05 |work=The Hindu |url-access=subscription |archive-date=5 December 2023 |access-date=6 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205083844/https://www.thehindu.com/elections/telangana-assembly/2023-telangana-assembly-elections-winds-of-change-in-telangana/article67605464.ece?art=package |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Aftermath==
[[All India Congress Committee]] (AICC) named [[Revanth Reddy]] as the leader of Congress Party in Telangana, following the elected MLAs' resolution authorizing the AICC to nominate the leader, paving way for him to become the [[Chief Minister of Telangana]].<ref name="third term CM">{{Cite news |title=Revanth Reddy To Be Sworn In As Telangana Chief Minister Tomorrow |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/revanth-reddy-to-be-sworn-in-as-telangana-chief-minister-tomorrow-4640509 |date=2023-12-07 |work=NDTV |access-date=8 December 2023 |archive-date=8 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608112704/https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/revanth-reddy-to-take-oath-as-telangana-chief-minister-today-sonia-gandhi-rahul-gandhi-to-attend-4640509 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 7 December 2023, he took oath as the [[List of chief ministers of Telangana|Chief Minister of Telangana]], thus becoming the second person to hold the post.{{Efn|He is the second person to serve as CM, while being the third CM of the state, as K. Chandrashekar Rao served two terms.}}
